questions.title: Which driver will rank second in the Formula One drivers' championship immediately after the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix?
questions.background: The drivers' championship standings reflect cumulative points earned during the season, with ties resolved under Formula One's championship rules.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The post-race drivers' championship standings published by the FIA or Formula One. Resolution : Resolve to the driver ranked second in the championship standings following the Belgian Grand Prix scheduled for July 19, 2026, before any subsequent race takes place. Accepted Answer Format : The driver's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Post-Silverstone British GP (July 5, Reuters/FIA) turns the post-Spa P2 standings race into a pure two-driver contest with a significant structural advantage for George Russell. Charles Leclerc won behind the safety car while Russell stayed out to finish P2 (+18) ahead of Lewis Hamilton in P3 (+15, stewards took no further action on his yellow-flag investigation after Ferrari's late pitstop dropped him behind Russell), and Kimi Antonelli scored 0 (P16 after a front-left wheel shield kerb failure and 5s track limits penalty). With only ONE non-sprint race left before resolution (Belgian GP, July 19, max 25 pts, no fastest-lap point), standings are: Antonelli 179 (5 wins), Russell 154 (2 wins), Hamilton 147 (1 win), Leclerc 108 (1 win). Antonelli is mathematically guaranteed P1 (even a Russell win + Antonelli 0 ties at 179, which Antonelli wins 5-3 on win countback), and Leclerc (max 133) is mathematically eliminated—removing Antonelli's 0.005 tail completely. Russell expanded his lead over Hamilton from +4 to +7 pts AND holds the win-countback tiebreak (2 vs 1), meaning Hamilton must outscore Russell by >=8 pts at Spa (or win Spa while Russell finishes P2 and win P2-finish countback, where Russell already holds multiple P2s including Spain and Silverstone). Monte Carlo Spa simulations blending Mercedes's power-circuit edge (9/9 poles in 2026) with Ferrari's strong high-speed Silverstone form (2 wins in last 3 races) and ~9-10% DNF/rain chaos place Russell at 68-73% (baseline 0.70, up from 0.63) and Hamilton at 0.30 (down from 0.365).

local_articles.title: Russell says serious issue slowing his car, rules out driving style
local_articles.snippet: SPA-FRANCORCHAMPS, Belgium, July 18 - George Russell ruled out driving style as a factor in being out-qualified yet again by championship-leading Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli on Saturday and said his car was being slowed by a mystery issue. Antonelli, 25 points clear of closest rival Russell in the Formula One standings, took his sixth pole in 10 rounds at the Belgian Grand Prix and the 19-year-old Italian will be chasing his sixth win in Sunday's race. Russell will start third thanks to McLaren's Lando Norris having a 10-place grid penalty after qualifying ahead of him. “It could be worse, but it could be much better," said Russell. "Yesterday, I was losing eight tenths on the straights, and today I am losing four tenths. It is a step in the right direction. questions.title: Who will be appointed head of Syria’s National Security Bureau in July 2026?
questions.background: The National Security Bureau oversees Syria’s security agencies.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official Syrian government announcement or reporting by the Syrian state news agency SANA identifying the person appointed head of the National Security Bureau during July 2026. Resolution Date : The date the appointment is publicly announced. Accepted Answer Format : The appointee’s full name.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-07-15 major breaking development (The National July 15, Independent Arabia July 15, Yalla Syria News/Aksalser July 14): Three independent outlets citing Syrian and regional security officials confirm that President Ahmed al-Sharaa carried out a senior security reshuffle following the July 2 and July 7 Damascus bombings (during President Macron's visit) and turf friction between the Interior Ministry and intelligence. Outgoing General Intelligence Director Major General Hussein al-Salama has been appointed head of the National Security Bureau/Apparatus/Council (Arabic: 'رئيساً لجهاز الأمن القومي' in Independent Arabia & Aksalser; 'head of the National Security Council' in The National), while former Deputy Interior Minister Abdulqader al-Tahhan (Abu Billal al-Quds) replaces him as General Intelligence chief. Because The National notes Damascus has not yet issued the formal SANA announcement required by resolution criteria, we surge Hussein al-Salama from 0.18 -> 0.85 while keeping a calibrated 15% residual (0.04 Abdulqader al-Tahhan, 0.04 Anas Khattab, 0.02 Murhaf Abu Qasra, 0.01 Ali Noureddine al-Naasan, 0.04 other) for any formal decree reversal, delay, or distinct bureau naming.

questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Formula One's official results for the final practice session at the Hungarian Grand Prix Resolution Date : July 25, 2026 Accepted Answer Format : Driver's full name (the driver credited with the fastest lap)
questions.current_reasoning: FP3 is substantially noisier than qualifying due to varied fuel loads, run plans, traffic, and red flags, so the top 5 sum to 0.74 rather than 1.0 (leaving 26% for Piastri—who was P2 in Barcelona FP3—Verstappen, Hadjar, and outliers). Mercedes has topped all known 2026 FP3 sessions and all 7 qualifyings, with George Russell fastest in Australia and Barcelona FP3 and Kimi Antonelli fastest in Japan FP3. Charles Leclerc (P3 in all three known FP3s), Lando Norris (Hungaroring historically favors McLaren's high-downforce strength), and 8-time Hungary winner Lewis Hamilton lead the chasing pack a month out.

questions.title: Which circuit will Formula One announce as the replacement venue for the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix?
questions.background: The Bahrain Grand Prix originally scheduled for April 2026 was cancelled amid conflict in the Middle East.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Formula One's first official announcement after May 1, 2026 identifying a replacement host circuit for the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix. Resolution Conditions : The announcement must occur by December 31, 2026. Resolution is based on the announced venue, regardless of whether the race is subsequently held or receives final regulatory approval. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the circuit.
questions.current_reasoning: After Bahrain and Saudi Arabia were cancelled for April due to the Iran war, F1 signed a 5-year deal on April 24 bringing Istanbul Park back from 2027, and on May 7 FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem explicitly floated Istanbul Park stepping in early for 2026 pending FIA homologation, with a summer decision expected—and it fits the Oct 2-4 Baku-to-Singapore gap geographically. Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari (Imola) is F1's primary already-homologated reserve venue whose mayor reiterated readiness in late May, while Algarve International Circuit (Portimao) holds a valid Grade 1 licence and a 2027-28 deal. Sepang (next to Singapore) and Circuit Paul Ricard are smaller candidates, leaving 15% for other Grade 1 venues or surprise double-headers.

questions.title: Who will win the 2026 Formula One Hungarian Grand Prix?
questions.background: The Hungarian Grand Prix is a round of the Formula One World Championship.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The official race classification published by Formula One or the FIA. Resolution : Resolve to the driver classified as the winner of the Hungarian Grand Prix scheduled for July 26, 2026. This concerns the Grand Prix itself, not any sprint race. Accepted Answer Format : The winning driver's full name.

local_articles.title: Antonelli fastest, Hamilton crashes in final Belgian GP practice
local_articles.snippet: SPA-FRANCORCHAMPS, Belgium, July 18 - Formula One leader Kimi Antonelli lapped fastest for Mercedes in final practice for the Belgian Grand Prix on Saturday, while Lewis Hamilton crashed his Ferrari in the dying seconds of the session at Spa-Francorchamps. Italian Antonelli, 19, clocked a best time of one minute 45.990 seconds, 0.139 quicker than McLaren's reigning world champion Lando Norris. Red Bull's Max Verstappen was third on the timesheets with Antonelli's teammate and closest title rival George Russell fourth. Hamilton was fifth fastest but left his mechanics with a race against time to repair the car after he went off into the gravel at Fagnes and clouted the tyre wall, smashing the rear wing and suspension and sending debris across the track as the car bounced in the air.
